objective: Bring every DevArch service-library Compose definition to a verified current stable image policy and a documented production-ready operational baseline, while providing safe repeatable tooling to discover, review, apply, validate, and roll back future container image updates.

in: All 175 services-library/**/compose.yml definitions and their service-owned configuration files
Container image inventory, upstream release/version policy, lifecycle/EOL assessment, immutable digest strategy, and update evidence

Production-readiness controls appropriate to each image: secret injection, loopback exposure, persistent storage, health/readiness, restart/dependency behavior, least privilege, bounded logging/resources, graceful shutdown, and documented exceptions
A tested script under scripts/services/ that discovers candidates and safely applies explicitly approved image/tag/digest updates
Catalog validation, regression tests, CI checks, operator documentation, migration notes, and completion reporting
out: Application workspaces under apps/ and generated backups
Automatic unattended production deployment or restart of running containers
Secret generation, secret rotation, or committing real credentials
Blind adoption of prerelease/nightly tags or unreviewed major-version migrations
Guaranteeing production suitability of upstream application code beyond the Compose deployment boundary
Kubernetes, Helm, Swarm, or cloud-provider deployment definitions

constraints: Preserve Podman Compose compatibility and the existing canonical category/service/compose.yml layout.
Treat latest stable as an upstream-specific policy decision; do not infer correctness from lexical tag ordering or blindly select the numerically largest registry tag.
Replace floating latest or untagged references; record explicit exceptions when an upstream publishes no stable versioned image.
Use immutable manifest digests where registry support permits while retaining a human-readable version tag.
Never place real or reusable secrets in tracked files; required secret values must use explicit environment or file indirection and fail closed when absent.
Stateful major upgrades require upstream migration/backup notes and must not be represented as safe in-place changes without evidence.
Hardening controls must be capability-aware: read-only filesystems, non-root users, dropped capabilities, and resource controls require compatibility validation or a documented exception.
Updater mutations must be targeted, reviewable, atomic, dry-run capable, and followed by Compose plus repository validation; the tool must not start or restart services.
Preserve unrelated user changes and avoid broad YAML reserialization that destroys anchors, comments, ordering, or formatting.
Use authoritative upstream releases and registry metadata; record unavailable, rate-limited, archived, or ambiguous sources as explicit blockers rather than guessing.
The full catalog is too large for one undifferentiated change: update in risk-based batches with current evidence and review at each boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A deterministic inventory covers every Compose definition and every image reference, recording canonical service ID, Compose service name, current reference, authoritative upstream/release source, version policy, candidate stable version, digest availability, support/EOL status, confidence, and required migration review.

Every image reference is either an explicit reviewed stable version with immutable digest where supported or a documented, machine-checkable exception; no accidental latest, untagged, prerelease, or registry-ambiguous reference remains.

A tested updater supports catalog-wide check/report and explicitly targeted apply workflows, dry-run, exact old-reference preconditions, registry digest resolution, atomic writes, concise diffs, validation, failure rollback, and nonzero exit on ambiguity or partial failure without starting containers.

A versioned production-readiness policy and validator assess each Compose service for required-secret handling, network exposure, durable storage, health checks, restart/dependency behavior, logging bounds, resource guidance, graceful shutdown, privilege/capability posture, and justified per-image exceptions.

All low-risk stateless and infrastructure definitions are updated to reviewed current stable versions and brought into compliance with the production-readiness policy without breaking catalog conventions.

All stateful database, storage, messaging, search, and registry definitions are updated with explicit compatibility, backup, migration, persistence, and rollback notes plus production-readiness controls.

All complex multi-container, project, ERP, workflow, collaboration, security, and CI stacks are reconciled with authoritative upstream deployment guidance, coherent component versions, dependency health ordering, required secret inputs, and documented upgrade/rollback procedures.

Every changed definition passes YAML parsing, Podman Compose configuration validation where prerequisites are available, catalog validation, policy validation, and focused regression tests; unavailable runtime checks are reported as gaps and not counted as passes.

Operator documentation explains version semantics, production-ready versus local defaults, update/check/apply/review/rollback commands, stateful upgrade cautions, exceptions, and the recurring maintenance workflow.

A final machine-generated coverage report proves that all 175 definitions and all image references were dispositioned, identifies residual exceptions/blockers, and maps each risk batch to current verification and explicit model self-review evidence.

assessment.reason: This is a critical, catalog-wide migration spanning 175 Compose definitions, 201 Compose services, 199 image references, stateful data migrations, upstream compatibility research, security boundaries, and durable update automation. A missed definition or unsafe major upgrade could cause data loss or unreliable deployments.
surfaces: 201 Compose service entries and 199 image references
173 currently unique image references with mixed tag schemes
Stateful volumes and major-version migration boundaries
Multi-image application stacks requiring coherent release sets
Registry APIs, authoritative upstream release metadata, and rate limits
Podman Compose behavior and external microservices-net contract
Tracked configuration files, default credentials, privileges, ports, and secrets
Catalog discovery/tests and new scripts/services tooling
Operator workflow, CI, audit evidence, and rollback documentation
unknowns: Which host architectures and Podman/Compose provider versions must be supported beyond the current repository guidance
Whether production-ready resource limits should be enforced defaults or documented sizing recommendations for all service classes
Which services are actively relied upon versus showcase-only, affecting smoke-test depth and deprecation choices
Registry authentication/rate-limit availability during full candidate and digest resolution
Upstream projects whose newest releases require irreversible schema or storage migrations
Images with non-semantic, calendar, component-specific, or moving tag schemes
Archived, renamed, split, or commercially gated upstream projects
Whether all upstream images support rootless, non-root, read-only, or dropped-capability operation

practices.reason: Complete catalog coverage and authoritative version semantics must be established before bulk mutation so no image or migration boundary is missed.
The updater and policy validator mutate or gate 175 definitions, so failure, ambiguity, formatting preservation, atomicity, and rollback behavior require fixture-first automated tests.

practices.practice: Risk-batched migration with security and operations review
practices.reason: Stateless, stateful, and complex stacks have materially different upgrade, secret, health, privilege, and rollback risks and must not be handled as one mechanical version bump.
Final qualification must prove total catalog coverage, policy compliance, documentation accuracy, and explicit residual gaps after all batches land.

obligations.text: Run deterministic inventory/policy checks over the complete catalog and perform an explicit source-bound self-review for omissions, unsupported assumptions, and unsafe version selection.

Demonstrate updater behavior with fixture-based red/green tests covering dry-run, targeted apply, digest resolution seams, ambiguity, stale old references, atomic failure, rollback, validation failure, and formatting preservation.
Run production-readiness policy tests and a full-catalog baseline, with source-bound review of rule safety, false positives, exception schema, and Podman Compose compatibility.

verification.kind: policy validator tests and baseline review

obligations.text: Validate every low-risk/stateless batch and review image provenance, breaking changes, hardening compatibility, Compose output, and rollback notes before completion.
Validate every stateful batch and review upstream migration paths, data layout, backup/restore instructions, health behavior, version/digest provenance, and rollback limits before completion.

verification.kind: stateful batch validation and migration review

obligations.text: Validate every complex stack and review coherent component versions, upstream deployment parity, secret inputs, dependency ordering, health, persistent state, and rollback procedures before completion.

Run integrated repository and catalog qualification, regenerate the complete coverage report, verify documented commands, and perform an explicit source-bound self-review of all acceptance criteria and residual exceptions.

work.title: Inventory every image and define version/update policy

testing.reason: This task establishes a data inventory and policy; deterministic full-catalog coverage and schema checks are the useful qualification boundary.

work.title: Build safe image check and update tooling

testing.reason: Mutation safety, ambiguity rejection, exact preconditions, formatting preservation, atomic rollback, and registry failure behavior should be driven by failing fixtures before implementation.

work.title: Implement production-readiness policy, validator, and exception model

testing.reason: Policy rules will gate the entire catalog and need fixtures for compatible controls, justified exceptions, invalid secrets, exposure, persistence, health, privilege, and false-positive boundaries.

work.title: Update and harden low-risk stateless and infrastructure services

testing.reason: Apply the established tooling and policy in reviewable category batches, then run focused plus full-catalog validation after each batch.

work.title: Update and harden stateful data services

testing.reason: Stateful changes require upstream migration research and batch qualification of persistence, backup, restore, health, and rollback behavior rather than synthetic unit tests alone.

work.title: Reconcile and harden complex multi-container stacks

testing.reason: Complex stacks must be checked as coherent upstream-defined systems, with rendered Compose and targeted smoke validation where prerequisites permit.

work.title: Integrate qualification, recurring maintenance, and operator documentation

testing.reason: Final qualification should combine all incremental evidence with one current full-catalog audit, repository test run, documentation command checks, and acceptance-to-evidence review.

decisions.text: Separate candidate discovery from mutation: catalog-wide checks may propose updates, but applying a change requires an explicit reviewed target and exact old-reference precondition.
decisions.basis: Registry tag ordering and latest labels are not reliable enough for unattended major upgrades, especially for stateful and multi-image services.

decisions.text: Use human-readable explicit stable tags plus immutable manifest digests where supported, with machine-checkable exceptions for registries or upstreams that cannot provide them.
decisions.basis: Tags communicate intended versions while digests make deployment inputs reproducible.

decisions.text: Define production readiness as a validated operational baseline with capability-aware exceptions, not as blindly applying every hardening knob to every upstream image.
decisions.basis: Many vendor images require writable paths, fixed users, capabilities, or specific startup behavior; unsupported blanket controls can reduce reliability.

decisions.text: Partition implementation into stateless, stateful, and complex-stack risk batches.
decisions.basis: The catalog size and migration risk make a single bulk commit/review unsafe and difficult to roll back.

risks.text: Newest major versions can require destructive or one-way data migrations.
risks.mitigation: Require authoritative migration and backup/restore notes, explicit stateful review, and rollback limitations before updating each affected service.

risks.text: Registry tags may be moving, incomparable, rate-limited, architecture-specific, or inconsistent with upstream releases.
risks.mitigation: Use upstream-specific policies, manifest digests, confidence/status fields, caching, and fail-closed blockers rather than lexical guessing.

risks.text: Blanket non-root/read-only/capability/resource settings can break vendor images or make health checks unreliable.
risks.mitigation: Test controls per image class and require narrow documented exceptions with reasons and review dates.

risks.text: The repository currently contains convenience credentials and local defaults that may be mistaken for production-safe configuration.
risks.mitigation: Move required secrets to explicit environment/file inputs, fail closed, provide non-secret examples, and clearly distinguish local convenience from production operation.

risks.text: Broad YAML rewrites can silently alter anchors, scalar types, ordering, or multi-container relationships.
risks.mitigation: Use exact scalar replacement with parse-before/parse-after validation, atomic writes, concise diffs, and formatting-preservation fixtures.

risks.text: Full runtime smoke testing of 175 definitions is expensive and may require unavailable memory, architectures, credentials, or external services.
risks.mitigation: Use layered validation, risk-based representative smokes, prerequisite reporting, and explicit gaps; never convert unavailable checks into passes.

risks.text: Upstream projects may be archived, renamed, commercially gated, or no longer publish maintained images.
risks.mitigation: Record lifecycle status and choose an explicit hold, replacement proposal, or deprecation decision rather than silently retaining an unsafe version.
